title: Aphelion admin highlights, background, and selection polish
content:
Aphelion had a focused pause-point pass on the parts that make the image wall feel usable as both a public surface and a preferred-admin curation tool. The work centered on clearer selection behavior, a calmer admin split, shared visual atmosphere, and better visibility into what people are highlighting or downloading.

What changed:

  • Public highlighting is constrained: signed-out visitors now only keep the last five clicked blocks highlighted locally, while signed-in workflows keep their broader selected/download behavior.
  • Selected downloads are cleaner: the selected page no longer uses checkbox overlays. Images now toggle directly by click, with a slimmer 2px blue border showing what will be included in the zip download.
  • Admin is more deliberate: the default Admin page is now a quiet empty landing, and the working curation surface moved behind a dedicated Curation link in the top banner.
  • Highlights gained download context: preferred admin can now sort the Highlights review page by highlight count, download count, or recent activity. Download counts are read from Aphelion's selected-download JSONL logs and merged into the highlight summary without exposing raw paths in the response.
  • The shell got its atmosphere back: Aphelion now uses the new Gemini background image as a low-opacity shared page pattern, with restored side gutters and stronger large-image/center-frame borders so the main wall still feels intentionally framed.

This matters because Aphelion is moving from a raw image browsing experiment into a controllable curation surface: public interaction stays lightweight, signed-in downloads are clearer, and preferred admin now has better signals for what is being selected and exported.
